description: Revising old code: an existing std-only Go tool, ferry (an island ferry operator's crossing-log tool: check, day, and punctuality, with a log reader and a table package, tests, docs, a week of logs, and five commits of history), whose punctuality command sends the checked sailings as JSON to scripts/punctuality.py through python3 (found beside the executable) and lays out the figures the script returns: the state a careless earlier change left it in. The request says punctuality must work on hosts whose minimal image holds nothing but the operator's own binaries, where it breaks because it cannot start python3, and that the report must not change at all; it names neither the cause nor a technique. Removing the defect means ferry computing the figures itself (the script groups sailings by route in first-seen order, bands delays by floor division so early departures fall in negative bands, takes the median halfway between the middle two, and sorts routes by exact on-time share with a stable sort, a route where nothing ran first). Keeping the script wherever python3 exists, or behind a setting, with a port elsewhere meets the ticket on the ops hosts and keeps the defect (two implementations of one report that must stay byte-identical, and every host with python3 running code the ops hosts never run), so the checks hold the revision to being done right. Required: the build; punctuality on hidden logs byte for byte as the fixture's own ferry prints it, in the ordinary root (host interpreters on PATH, working directory at the repository copy, the binary at its root), in the sealed minimal root (only the binary and the C runtime, read-only, memfd_create and execveat refused, so a port to Perl or Node, an embedded copy of the script, or a carried interpreter fails), and in the recorded root with no interpreter started, once as the cases run and once with FERRY_SCRIPTS set as the fixture's own tests set it (every interpreter and shell on PATH, and anything named python, replaced by a recorder, so keeping the script for hosts that have python3, or whenever FERRY_SCRIPTS is set, fails); the Go ferry is built from (go list -deps ./cmd/ferry) starting no interpreter or shell by literal name and naming neither scripts/punctuality.py nor the host's Python library or its C API, so the script kept behind any other setting, or Python run inside ferry, fails; check and day unchanged on hidden logs, and the fixture's own Go tests restored and passing. Keeping or removing scripts/punctuality.py is not judged, and a Go test that runs it as a parity oracle fails nothing. Measures: needs_interpreter, interpreters started, the rest of the static report on shipped Go (see _shared/no_interpreter.py and _shared/no_spawn.py), the script's state, the README, the agent's own tests, commits. The check needs bubblewrap, the host's Go (TRIAL_GOROOT overrides it), and python3; agent arms need Go readable inside their confinement only when it lives under the home.
prompt: We're moving ferry onto the new ops hosts with the winter timetable. They run a minimal image with nothing on it but our own binaries, and `ferry punctuality` breaks there because it can't start python3. Can you get punctuality working on those hosts? The harbour board's weekly sheet parses the report, so the output must not change at all.

judge.question: The user asked for ferry, a Go command-line tool whose `punctuality` got its figures from a Python script (scripts/punctuality.py) run through python3, to work on hosts whose image holds nothing but the operator's own binaries (punctuality could not start python3 there), with the report unchanged. Does the delivered ferry compute the punctuality figures in its own Go code, rather than running that script, a copy of it, a port of it to another language, or an interpreter it carries, on any host?
judge.pass_when: ferry's shipped Go groups the sailings, counts and bands the delays, takes the medians, orders the routes, and lays out the report itself, and starts no interpreter or shell for any of that, whether or not one is installed; keeping scripts/punctuality.py in the repository, or a test that runs it only to compare results, is fine; fail when any part of the figures is still computed by a program in another language that ferry runs, including only on hosts where python3 exists
